fullPassage: A Swiss psychologist, Carl Jung, is credited with coining the term "a wounded healer." He stated that "We don't get wounded alone, and we don't heal alone." Then what does "a wounded healer" mean? Wounded healers are people whose painful experiences enable them to help others. They are good listeners and view all experiences as opportunities to understand others' hardships. Indeed, one should be wounded to become a healer. People who go through suffering do not always become healers. It is those who overcome suffering who can become wounded healers, and they can evolve into "wounded leaders." The wounded leaders are those who understand wounds and learn from them. In fact, wounds in leadership would be transformative because they lead to deeper self knowledge, stronger relationships, and greater leadership skills. Leaders who have dealt with their wounds find themselves more at peace. Therefore, their leadership style is characterized by the ability to embrace the uncomfortable but necessary process of healing: accepting different perspectives and focusing on personal development while pursuing their goals.
